name: bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline
title: Reduced-order tissue-mechanics baseline
claim: The homogeneous prism model recovers the paper's confinement regimes: a fixed-volume cell grows TALL under a stiff, slowly-relaxing basement membrane and SPREADS flat under a soft, fast-relaxing one, with cell height rising monotonically along both the BM stiffness and the BM relaxation axes of the Figure 1G map.
experiment: Run the reduced-order TissuePrismProcess (one representative fixed-volume prism cell; basal area set by proliferation pushing against a viscoelastic BM; cell height = volume / basal area) over a BM-stiffness x BM-relaxation grid at a fixed doubling time (stiffness in {0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0}, relaxation in {1, 5, 20, 50}, doubling_time 5.0), integrating 40 steps of dt 0.2. Read the final cell height, the relative confinement, and the BM reaction stress at each grid point, and check the regime ordering and the monotonic trends against Barrientos Figure 1G.
result: The regime map reproduces cleanly and deterministically. Cell height rises monotonically with BM stiffness at every relaxation value and with BM relaxation at every stiffness value (both axes strictly non-decreasing across the full grid). The stiff, slowly-relaxing corner (stiffness 5.0, relaxation 50.0) confines the cell to height 0.630, while the soft, fast-relaxing corner (stiffness 0.1, relaxation 1.0) lets it spread to height 0.380 -- a 1.66x taller cell under confinement. The mechanism is the BM reaction stress: it reaches 2.64 (reduced units) in the confined corner and only 0.031 in the spread corner, so the stiff/slow membrane resists basal-area growth and keeps the cell tall. Heights are dimensionless and all below the initial height of 1.0 (the cell spreads from its starting shape as it proliferates); the reproduced result is the RELATIVE regime topology and the monotonic trends, not an absolute height in microns.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: A stable, separable confinement regime map (height monotone in both stiffness and relaxation) is the effective-BM reference for the spatial Tyssue studies (R4/R5) and the shape-prediction endpoint of the turnover pipeline (R6).

question: How do basement-membrane stiffness and relaxation, relative to the proliferation (doubling) time, control growth-dependent epithelial confinement?

purpose.question: How do basement-membrane stiffness and relaxation, relative to the proliferation (doubling) time, control growth-dependent epithelial confinement?
purpose.mechanism: A fixed-volume prism cell proliferates (its preferred basal area grows), pushing against a viscoelastic BM whose rest area relaxes toward the current area over a relaxation time. A stiffer or slower-relaxing BM builds more reaction stress, resisting spreading, so the cell stays tall (confined); a soft or fast-relaxing BM lets the area grow and the cell spread flat.
purpose.expected_outcome: A separable confinement regime map: cell height increasing with BM stiffness and with the relaxation/doubling ratio, reproducing the four regimes of Barrientos Figure 1G.

hypothesis: Reimplementing the paper's fixed-volume prism / surface-tension tissue model with a viscoelastic BM reproduces Figure 1G's four stiffness-relaxation regimes and the 1H-J confinement trajectories, with the regime boundary set by the ratio of BM relaxation time to doubling time.
objective: Reimplement the paper's fixed-volume prism/surface-tension tissue model and viscoelastic BM; sweep relative stiffness and the relaxation/doubling-time ratio; compare qualitatively and quantitatively to Barrientos et al. Figure 1G-J.
description:
Direct reproduction of the paper's homogeneous tissue-mechanics result (Barrientos Fig 1). A
fixed-volume prism/surface-tension cell model is coupled to a viscoelastic BM; the relative
BM stiffness and the relaxation/doubling-time ratio are swept to recover the regime topology
(reconstructed basal area and cell height, reversibility, regime boundaries). This is the P1
homogeneous reference the spatial Tyssue studies (R4-R5) are later compared against; it uses
an effective constitutive BM, not the explicit collagen network.
key_assumptions: One representative cell of fixed volume (volume=1, area0=1); cell height = volume/basal_area.
The BM is an effective viscoelastic constitutive element (an area stiffness + a rest-area relaxation time), not the explicit collagen IV network.
Proliferation grows the preferred basal area exponentially on the doubling timescale; basal area relaxes toward preferred, resisted by the BM reaction stress.
Homogeneous (non-spatial): one prism, no neighbours -- the reference the spatial R4/R5 models are compared against.
Reduced units: stiffness, relaxation, time and stress are dimensionless; no calibration to microns / pascals / hours is claimed.

model_assumptions_declaration.preferred_vs_realized: explicit — a growing PREFERRED basal area; realized area lags it (inferred prism height = volume/area)
model_assumptions_declaration.load_control_vs_reaction: reaction — BM reaction stress resists spreading; BM is an imposed EFFECTIVE viscoelastic law, not explicit collagen
model_assumptions_declaration.growth_vs_division: proliferation grows the preferred area (exponential); NO explicit cell division
model_assumptions_declaration.calibration_limits: reduced units; no calibration to microns/pascals/hours; relative regime topology only

meeting_alignment_2026_10_20.note: Reformulate growth as an evolving PREFERRED cell area/volume (or preferred cell number), NOT imposed realized geometry — the meeting's key modeling constraint. Keep growth separate from cell division for the MVP; the paper uses proliferation, so distinguish faithful reproduction from the no-division growth extension.

baseline.name: bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline
baseline.note: A homogeneous tissue model: one representative cell of fixed volume whose basal area is set by proliferation pulling against a viscoelastic basement membrane, with cell height following from volume over area. The four confinement regimes of the paper's Figure 1 fall out of how membrane stiffness compares with its relaxation time and the cell doubling time -- a stiff, slowly-relaxing membrane confines the cell into a tall shape, while a soft or fast-relaxing one lets it spread flat. This is the simple reference the spatial epithelial models are compared against.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if, across the stiffness x relaxation grid, cell height were NOT monotone along either axis, or if the stiff/slow corner were not taller than the soft/fast corner (a non-separating or inverted regime map), or if confinement did not track the BM reaction stress. Any of these would show the reduced-order model does not reproduce the Fig 1G regime topology. The deterministic contracts in tests/test_tissue_prism.py would fail in that case.

if_primary_tests_pass.implementation_status: The reduced-order baseline runs end-to-end and separates the confinement regimes.
if_primary_tests_pass.biological_validation: Qualitative match to Fig 1G: height monotone in BM stiffness and relaxation; stiff+slow confines, soft+fast spreads.
pipeline_unblocks: R4/R5 spatial Tyssue studies -- this is their effective-BM reference.
R6 turnover->shape pipeline -- this prism model is its shape-prediction endpoint.

diagnose: Mobility too high -- the cell spreads before the BM can resist; lower mobility or lengthen the run.
Relaxation >> run length -- the viscoelastic BM never builds stress; extend steps or shorten relaxation.
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: Do not use as the R4/R5 reference until the regime map separates.

limitations: Reduced units throughout: stiffness, relaxation, time and stress are dimensionless; no calibration to microns / pascals / hours.
Heights are all below the initial height of 1.0 -- the cell spreads overall as it proliferates; the reproduced result is the RELATIVE regime ordering, not absolute confinement.
Homogeneous single cell: no spatial neighbours, no explicit collagen network -- the explicit-BM comparison is R4/R5.
The 1H-J reversibility trajectories are not yet reproduced; only the 1G regime topology + monotonic trends are claimed here.
The grid is a 5x4 corner sweep at a single doubling time; a finer map over the relaxation/doubling ratio is a follow-up (the viz heatmap renders a denser 12x12 grid for presentation).

config.title: Confinement across BM stiffness × relaxation/doubling, with regime boundary + trajectories (cf. Fig 1)
config.caption: Reduced-order epithelial model predicts cell confinement across the two dimensionless axes the paper uses — BM stiffness relative to the cell and BM relaxation time / proliferation (doubling) time. Panel A maps confinement (h/h₀) with the confinement=1 boundary drawn and the three sampled regimes marked; panels B–D show representative basal-area growth trajectories for the soft/fast, intermediate and stiff/slow corners. This is our analytic reimplementation of the Barrientos Fig 1 model (not a simulation and not a digitized overlay of the published boundaries): the regime topology is consistent with Fig 1 — tall/confined in the stiff, slowly-relaxing corner — and a quantitative boundary overlay vs digitized Fig 1G is the open follow-up.

report.title: R1 -- reduced-order tissue confinement baseline (Fig 1G reproduction)
report.verdict: The homogeneous prism + viscoelastic-BM model reproduces Barrientos Figure 1G's confinement regime topology on a deterministic reduced-order run. Cell height rises monotonically along both the BM stiffness axis and the BM relaxation axis, and the stiff/slow corner confines the cell to 1.66x the height of the soft/fast corner. The confinement is mechanistically driven by the BM reaction stress (2.64 confined vs 0.031 spread). The reproduction is qualitative / relative (reduced units; heights below the initial shape); absolute shape and the 1H-J reversibility trajectories are out of scope for this baseline.
report.main_insight: A three-parameter reduced-order model (BM stiffness, BM relaxation, doubling time) is enough to recover the paper's confinement regime map: confinement emerges from a stiff or slow BM building reaction stress that resists proliferation-driven spreading.
report.caveat: Reduced units only (no microns/pascals/hours); the single-cell homogeneous model is the effective-BM reference for the spatial R4/R5 studies, not a spatial result itself.

findings.statement: The reduced-order prism + viscoelastic-BM model reproduces Figure 1G's confinement regime topology: cell height increases monotonically with BM stiffness and with BM relaxation, so a stiff, slowly-relaxing membrane confines the cell (height 0.630) and a soft, fast-relaxing one lets it spread (height 0.380).

evidence.observed: confined/spread height ratio 1.66; monotone non-decreasing along both grid axes

expected.range: taller cells under stiff/slow BM, flatter under soft/fast BM (Fig 1G)

findings.explanation: Height = volume/area; a stiff or slow BM resists basal-area growth, keeping the area small and the cell tall. The relaxation/doubling ratio sets which regime the cell lands in.
findings.next_action: use as the effective-BM reference for the spatial R4/R5 confinement studies

findings.statement: Confinement tracks the BM reaction stress: the confined corner carries stress 2.64 while the spread corner carries 0.031, so the regime ordering is set by how much reaction stress the BM can build against proliferation, not by the stiffness value alone.
findings.explanation: bm_stress = bm_stiffness * (area - BM rest area); a slow relaxation keeps the rest area lagging, sustaining stress.

findings.statement: All grid heights are below the initial height of 1.0: the cell spreads overall as it proliferates, so the reproduced quantity is the RELATIVE regime ordering and the monotone trends, not an absolute confinement in physical units.

evidence.observed: max grid height 0.630 < 1.0; the ordering (not the absolute value) is the result

findings.next_action: calibrate to microns / a doubling-time ratio when coupling to the spatial models

followup_proposals.title: Reproduce the Fig 1H-J confinement reversibility trajectories
followup_proposals.motivation: This baseline reproduces the 1G steady-state regime map but not the 1H-J trajectories (ramp the BM property, then reverse it, and read the height path). Add a time-varying BM protocol and check reversibility/hysteresis.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: The viscoelastic BM should show a relaxation-time-dependent hysteresis as the property is ramped and reversed.

resolved_uncertainties: A 3-parameter reduced-order model is sufficient to recover Fig 1G's confinement regimes.
The regime ordering is mechanistically the BM reaction stress, not the stiffness value in isolation.
remaining_uncertainties: Absolute cell shape in physical units -- reduced units only here.
The 1H-J reversibility trajectories -- not yet reproduced.

regression_compatibility.basis: The tissue_prism_baseline composite is registered and the reduced-order process runs cleanly; the behavior-test contracts pass deterministically in CI.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces Fig 1G's confinement regime topology qualitatively: cell height monotone in both BM stiffness and BM relaxation, stiff+slow confined (0.630) vs soft+fast spread (0.380).

explanatory_gain.basis: Identifies confinement as emergent from BM reaction stress resisting proliferation-driven spreading, and provides the effective-BM reference the spatial R4/R5 studies are compared against.

expert_questions: Calibration: should this reduced-order map be reported in physical units (microns height, pascals BM stiffness, hours relaxation/doubling) before it is used as the R4/R5 effective-BM reference, or is the dimensionless regime topology sufficient for the comparison?

Regime boundary: the paper frames the regimes by the relaxation/doubling RATIO; this sweep fixes doubling_time. Should the canonical map instead sweep the ratio explicitly (vary doubling_time too) to place the regime boundary?
